standard_prerequisites.name: Wigner transform
standard_prerequisites.statement: W[Q](x,xi) is the semiclassically scaled partial Fourier transform of Q in the relative variable.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof rewrites W[Q] as an inverse-scaled Fourier transform in the relative variable at source line 483.

standard_prerequisites.name: Plancherel's theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Fourier transform preserves the L2 norm.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the step that converts the L2 norm of the displayed Fourier transform into the L2 norm of Q (source line 484).

standard_prerequisites.name: Semiclassical scaling
standard_prerequisites.statement: The prefactor (2 pi hbar)^{-d/2} converts the quantum L2 norm into the classical one.
standard_prerequisites.use: It appears both in the statement and in the displayed rewriting of W[Q] at source line 483.

core_obligations: Rewrite the Wigner transform of Q as (2 pi hbar)^{-d} times the Fourier transform in xi of the rescaled product Q(x + ./2, x - ./2) (source lines 481-484).
Apply Plancherel's theorem to that Fourier transform, which converts the L2 norm over (x,xi) into the L2 norm of the rescaled two-variable function (source line 484).

Cancel the scaling: the prefactor of the transform and the Jacobian of the change of variables (x + y, x - y) combine to give the factor (2 pi hbar)^{-d/2} in front of the L2 norm of Q, which is the statement (source lines 475-477 and 484).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the Wigner transform with a scaled Fourier transform in the relative variable.
Apply Plancherel and cancel the semiclassical factors.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `L2normofWigner` at source lines 474-479: for Q in L2(R^d;C) the Wigner transform satisfies ||W[Q]||_{L2, x,xi} = (2 pi hbar)^{-d/2} ||Q||_{L2, x,y} = ||Q||_{L^2}. The proof (source lines 480-485) is short but it is a computation with two named ingredients that both have to be invoked in the right variable: the Wigner transform is first identified with a scaled Fourier transform in the relative variable xi of the product Q(x + ./2, x - ./2) (source line 483), and Plancherel is then applied in that same variable (source line 484). Getting the constant (2 pi hbar)^{-d/2} out requires matching the prefactor of the transform against the change of variables in the two-variable norm, which is exactly what the statement asserts and the proof does not spell out beyond the display.
